3. The Pesticide’s Bastard Son
In 1936, Gerhard Schrader was searching for a way to save crops from insects but ended up creating a substance that would instead end human lives with invisible efficiency. This compound was the first of its kind: odorless, colorless, and capable of overriding the nervous system to cause instant, fatal convulsions. It transformed chemical warfare from a battle of skin irritants to a biological death sentence. What was the first nerve agent synthesized in this tragic laboratory accident?
